content.thinking:
This intervention just describes what climate scientists actually do—measurement, modeling, ice cores, satellites—in a neutral, informational way, mostly building competence perception rather than addressing integrity or funding. Based on similar process-transparency texts, I'd expect a modest positive effect on trust, maybe 2-4 points, with the competence subscale showing the strongest gain.

Working through the individual outcomes: trust_multidimensional around 2.5, trust_post around 1.8 given anchoring, distrust_post slightly negative around -1.2. Funding perceptions and institutional trust get small bumps, maybe 1-1.5 points, with NASA's positive mention offset by dilution from mentioning federal government broadly. Belief, concern, and policy measures all land in the modest 0.5-1.5 range given anchoring effects, while behavioral measures and donation to AMS stay very small, under 0.1 points, since a methods-focused text doesn't strongly motivate action.

parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a purely descriptive, non-argumentative account of climate science methods (ice cores, satellites, CO2 observatories, modeling). Its main mechanism is boosting perceived COMPETENCE and, secondarily, openness/rigor, via concrete procedural detail and a vivid precision analogy; it says nothing about scientists' motives, funding incentives, consensus, or policy, so integrity/benevolence gains and downstream attitude shifts should be weaker. I therefore expect a modest positive effect on the primary multidimensional trust index (~2-3 points, driven mostly by the competence subscale), a somewhat smaller effect on the single-item trust measure because respondents anchor on their pre-treatment answer, and a smaller-magnitude reduction in distrust (distrust items are stickier and less responsive to competence information). Belief and concern should move only slightly since the text implies but never argues anthropogenic causation, and belief is also pre-anchored and near ceiling for most believers. Policy and behavior outcomes are two steps removed from the treatment, so I put them below 1 point; institutional trust gets a small lift (NASA/NOAA are implicitly validated) diluted by the federal-government item. Incentivized behaviors (real donation, real newsletter signup) are notoriously insensitive to a single reading, so I forecast a few cents and well under one percentage point, with the AMS donation getting a tiny nudge from the measurement/meteorology framing.
